sources.title: Lovable: Overview; What is not available on mobile
sources.locator: Overview; What is not available on mobile
sources.finding: Lovable provides native iOS and Android apps using the same account, projects and credits as its web app. Mobile has no offline editing, cannot create accounts or configure OAuth connectors, and omits narrow-screen preview tools.

sources.title: Lovable: Credits and usage
sources.finding: A workspace subscription pools build credits for its projects and collaborators. Free has daily allowances; paid plans add monthly subscription credits and top-ups.

sources.title: Lovable: How to use Build mode
sources.finding: Users describe a project or change in chat; the hosted builder explores the code, edits files and runs checks without a local environment setup.

sources.title: Lovable: Lovable MCP server
sources.finding: The official MCP server lets external AI tools interact with Lovable projects using authenticated tools.

sources.title: Lovable: Custom MCP servers
sources.finding: Lovable can connect to custom MCP servers so the agent can access external tools and information.

sources.title: Lovable: How to use Build mode
sources.finding: Natural-language prompts initiate project changes in the project chat. This is not proof of a separate issue backlog.

sources.title: Lovable: Review and edit a plan
sources.finding: Plan mode investigates without changing code and produces a plan users can edit, revise and approve before Build mode. Planning costs one credit plus any subagent research.

sources.title: Lovable: Project knowledge
sources.finding: Project knowledge provides persistent instructions and context for Lovable across project requests.

sources.title: Lovable: November 4, 2026: Dreaming
sources.finding: Paid-plan Dreaming checks memory and AGENTS.md rules against code and chat, rewrites or removes outdated notes and records AGENTS.md changes in chat and history. User-requested rules stay as written.

sources.title: Lovable: How subagents work
sources.finding: Read-only subagents can search files, inspect project code, perform lookups and browse the web, returning findings to the main agent. Their context is limited to their brief.

sources.title: Lovable: Can multiple subagents run at once?
sources.locator: Can multiple subagents run at once?
sources.finding: Lovable can run multiple read-only research subagents concurrently on independent questions. They cannot edit, create or delete project files.

sources.title: Lovable: Subagent types; How subagents work
sources.finding: Lovable starts Generic and Explore read-only subagents, displays their status and inspected steps, and receives their findings automatically. Subagents report to the main agent and do not communicate directly with each other.

sources.title: Lovable: Send follow-ups mid-build; Control the cost
sources.locator: Send follow-ups mid-build; Control the cost
sources.finding: Users can send steering follow-ups while a build runs or stop it. Credit exhaustion pauses work with resume or wrap-up options, and completed edits remain after a stop.

sources.title: Lovable: Draft statuses
sources.finding: The draft switcher shows working, updates available, new changes, needs input and failed states, with shared All drafts and My drafts views. This is draft navigation, not proof of an epic backlog.

sources.title: Lovable: How Lovable works on a goal
sources.locator: How Lovable works on a goal
sources.finding: A /goal Build message continues toward an outcome for up to ten hours, accepts follow-ups and still pauses for credit check-ins or needed access.

sources.title: Lovable: Overview; Offline use
sources.finding: Web and mobile clients operate on the same hosted projects and require an active network connection. The source does not establish that a build always continues after client disconnect.

sources.title: Lovable: Create a draft; Update a draft
sources.locator: Create a draft; Update a draft
sources.finding: Each draft is a separate project copy with its own chat and preview. Changes reach the main unpublished project only after acceptance; newer main changes can be brought into a draft. No container, VM or worktree boundary is asserted.

sources.title: Lovable: Accept the draft; Delete a draft
sources.locator: Accept the draft; Delete a draft
sources.finding: Accepted drafts enter project history. Deleting a draft removes its edits and cannot be undone. Process recovery after host loss is not documented here.

sources.title: Lovable: How long Lovable works on one message; Cost controls
sources.locator: How long Lovable works on one message; Cost controls
sources.finding: Build messages run up to ten hours and wrap up during the last half hour. Credit check-ins default to twenty credits and pause for a decision; the stop button halts work.

sources.title: Lovable: Tasks and execution visibility
sources.finding: Details view has a Timeline of tool calls and steps and a Changes tab showing resulting file edits.

sources.title: Lovable: Pricing
sources.finding: The response menu shows Credits used during execution and final cost after completion. There is no upfront estimate; credit charges depend on work and tools used.

sources.title: Lovable: Collaboration in a specific project
sources.finding: Invited project collaborators build in the same project using the owner workspace credits; each can work in a separate draft. This establishes shared editable projects, not simultaneous input ordering on one agent.

sources.title: Lovable: Project permissions; Workspace permissions
sources.finding: Project and workspace roles include Viewer, Editor, Admin and Owner with explicit edit, publish, member and billing permissions. Free plans lack admin roles.

sources.title: Lovable: Security and governance
sources.finding: SSO is included on Business and Enterprise; SCIM and organizations are Enterprise features.

sources.title: Lovable: Project permissions
sources.finding: Editors and above can publish by default. Enterprise workspace policies can require publishing approval or block public or external-collaborator publishing.

sources.title: Lovable: Tasks and execution visibility
sources.finding: The Details Timeline records build steps and tool calls and Changes shows edits. Retention and tamper resistance have not been independently verified.

sources.title: Lovable: Tasks and execution visibility
sources.finding: Users can inspect per-change summaries and file diffs through Details, then return to Preview. No timed guided-review fixture was run.

sources.title: Lovable: Tasks and execution visibility
sources.finding: Build results include file diffs and summaries in Details, with Timeline and Changes tabs.

sources.title: Lovable: Debugging and verification
sources.finding: Lovable has browser testing, frontend tests and edge-function verification; most verification tools run when requested. Access to these tools does not establish a mandatory passing gate.

sources.title: Lovable: GitHub connection types
sources.finding: GitHub Cloud and Enterprise connections provide two-way code sync, branch operations and pull-request creation.

sources.title: Lovable: Project permissions
sources.finding: Editors and above can publish, while Enterprise policies can require an approval or block publishing. The exact-revision gate was not tested.

sources.title: Lovable: Edit code
sources.finding: Every manual code save creates a version in project history and users can revert a broken edit.

sources.title: Lovable: Limited license; Intellectual property
sources.finding: Vendor-authored service terms grant limited access and reserve ownership of the platform and underlying software to Lovable. Generated project code is a separate scope.

sources.title: Lovable: Download your project codebase
sources.finding: Paid-plan editors can export the project as a ZIP; Git sync is available on all plans. Exported app code does not establish self-hosting of the Lovable ADE or portable chat history.

sources.title: Lovable: Security and governance
sources.finding: Business and Enterprise workspace data are excluded from AI training by default; Free and Pro can opt out per account. Training controls are not telemetry controls.
